card.name: Huyen Lallong
card.era: Ancient (recorded in Puya manuscripts; revived 20th c.)
card.tagline: Manipuri martial art of sword and spear, also called Thang-Ta
card.profile: Huyen Langlon (Meitei: huyen = war, langlon/lanlong = art/knowledge) is the martial-art-and-dance tradition of the Meitei people of Manipur, comprising Thang-Ta (armed combat, from thang = sword and ta = spear) and Sarit Sarak (unarmed combat) (Wikipedia, Huyen langlon). Its spectacular component includes the thangkairol (sword dance) and khousarol (spear dance), practised in ritual, demonstration and combat modes, and is closely intertwined with Manipuri ritual and classical dance (Wikipedia). The tradition's earliest records appear in Puya manuscripts such as the Chainarol-Puya; it was suppressed under British rule (1891-1947) and later revived (Wikipedia).
card.insight: The art's continuity was sustained by masters such as Gurumayum Gourakishor Sharma, who received the Padma Shri in 2009, underscoring its formal recognition as a living martial-cultural heritage of Manipur (Wikipedia).
